newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU wants to see report on British abattoirs.
newsitem.headline: EU wants to see report on British abattoirs.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday that a controversial British report on the state of British abattoirs appeared not to have been presented to the EU executive and that officials would like to see it.
The report, by the government's Meat Hygiene Service, was leaked to the Financial Times newspaper but was never officially published.
It concluded that the abattoirs were becoming breeding grounds for the E-coli organism that killed at least 20 people through food poisoning in Scotland.
"They are not aware of the report," Commission agriculture spokesman Gerard Kiely told reporters, referring to experts in the agriculture directorate general. "We will be asking for the report."
But Kiely added that from what he had read in the newspapers there appeared to be no surprises in the report.
"It is essentially along the lines our own inspectors found," he said.

Members of the inspection team which prepared the report said Ministry of Agriculture officials had told them to tone down some their findings which would have been very damaging to the meat industry.

The report, which was due to be published early last year, was held back after they refused. It would have coincided with the government's admission of a possible link between mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), and its human equivalent Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD).
The crisis over mad cow disease resulted in a European Union worldwide ban on British beef exports and crippled the British beef industry, costing it 3.5 billion pounds ($5.7 million).
